triage_method: Every one of the 90 namespace-2 rows was classified by direct evidence: (1) the 34 rows the manifest draft itself already flags with a `reclassify` proposal (compatibility_adapter / intentionally_excluded) are recorded verbatim as REUSED_OR_RECLASSIFY -- no fresh check fabricated for them; (2) of the remaining 56 case-spec'd rows, every julia_surface claim was checked against the actual loaded/greppable src/*.jl -- and, where the SAME underlying R function already has a real, previously-EXECUTED runtime verdict in a sibling area's frozen contract (postfit-1-batch-contract.json's coef/getLoadings/getREsd/getResidualCor/getResidualCov/loading_ci/gllvmTMB_diagnose rows; postfit-2-batch-contract.json's 39 rows, all backed by isdefined()+functional-probe runtime evidence), that prior verdict is deferred to rather than re-derived, to avoid contradicting or duplicating already-executed evidence; (3) the remaining 9 rows (bridge admission + 3 non-Gaussian family-bridge dispatch keys that genuinely have no sibling-area coverage) are built as this batch's EXECUTABLE_NOW cases.

cases.r_call: gllvmTMB(y ~ 1, family = gaussian(), num.lv = 2, data = dat)` on a small simulated dataset
cases.julia_surface: GLLVM.jl top-level fit entry point (`fit_gllvm`/family dispatch in `families/fit_gllvm.jl`) invoked via `gllvm_julia_fit` on the identical simulated data
comparands: log-likelihood to <=1e-6 (or documented tolerance for non-Gaussian Laplace)
cases.check: R gllvmTMB(value ~ 0 + trait + latent(...), family=gaussian()) native fit vs Julia fit_gaussian_gllvm(Y; K, X) on the identical Y: |loglik_R - loglik_Julia| and max|coef_R - coef_Julia|.

cases.r_call: gllvmTMB_wide(Y, X = NULL, family = gaussian(), num.lv = 2)` wide-matrix-input fit entry point
cases.julia_surface: Julia bridge's wide/matrix-input fit path (or documented rejection if wide-input is not yet exposed by the bridge)
comparands: log-likelihood parity to the equivalent long-format gllvmTMB() call
cases.check: R gllvmTMB_wide(Y_wide, d=K, family=gaussian()) loglik vs the SAME R session's gllvmTMB() long-format loglik on the transposed-equivalent data (both R-native; this case is an R-internal long-vs-wide consistency check, matching the manifest's own comparand 'log-likelihood parity to the equivalent long-format gllvmTMB() call').

cases.r_call: gllvm_julia_fit(data, formula, family = gaussian(), num.lv = 2, ...)` R-side entry point that dispatches into the Julia bridge
cases.julia_surface: the Julia-side fit function it calls into (`GLLVM.fit_gllvm`/family dispatch) plus the JuliaCall/JuliaConnectoR marshalling layer
comparands: returned log-likelihood and point estimates vs. the equivalent native R gllvmTMB() fit
cases.check: R-side: gllvm_julia_fit()'s own family-argument mapper (.gllvm_julia_family_scalar, sourced directly from R/julia-bridge.R, no gllvmTMB package build required) accepts family='gaussian' and resolves it to the bridge key 'gaussian'. Julia-side: the exact function gllvm_julia_fit marshals into, bridge_fit(y=Y, family='gaussian', d=K, X=X), is called directly on the identical Y and must succeed with loglik matching the CORE070-NAMESPACE2-GLLVMTMB-NATIVE-FIT case's Julia oracle. Scope note: as above, this proves both halves of the admission path work without a live JuliaCall round trip from inside R.
cases.tolerance: <=1e-6 loglik delta vs the native-fit case

cases.r_call: gllvm_julia_setup(...)` environment/session bootstrap (Julia binary discovery, package activation)
cases.julia_surface: successful activation of the `GLLVM.jl` project environment it targets
comparands: setup completes without error on a clean R session
reported Julia/GLLVM.jl version strings are consistent with the pinned bridge contract
cases.check: R-side: gllvm_julia_setup()'s own preconditions (Sys.which('julia') resolves; the GLLVM_JL_PATH env var / gllvmTMB.GLLVM.jl.path option would resolve to this checkout) are satisfiable, checked without invoking JuliaCall itself. Julia-side: the already-running child process independently confirms realpath(Base.pkgdir(GLLVM)) == realpath(pwd()) and reports VERSION -- i.e. exactly the preconditions gllvm_julia_setup's jl_path would need are met in this checkout. Scope note: this does NOT execute a live JuliaCall session from within R (see contract rationale); it is a preconditions-satisfied check, not a full R-embeds-Julia round trip.

needs_new_julia_surface.missing_surface: GLLVM.jl's @formula front-end (src/formula.jl) has no term-recognizer for 'gr(...)'
needs_new_julia_surface.reason: src/formula.jl (module header: 'Slices 1-2 of the formula-front-end design spec') implements only plain StatsModels covariate/interaction terms; grep -rniE '"gr"' src/formula.jl src/bridge.jl: 0 hits for a term-name dispatch. gllvmTMB's brms-sugar keyword grammar (gr() and its 19 siblings, all defined in R/brms-sugar.R, R/kernel-keywords.R or R/traits-keyword.R) is parsed entirely on the R side into structured arguments (K, mode, tree, kernel spec, ...) before ever reaching the Julia bridge; bridge_fit/fit_gllvm receive those already-decomposed keyword arguments directly, never the literal term text. rationale_notes: gllvm_julia_setup / gllvm_julia_fit are scoped to prove BOTH halves of the admission path (R-side argument/family validation logic, and the exact Julia function the R side marshals into) work correctly, WITHOUT executing a live JuliaCall session embedded inside the R process. A prior incident in this same campaign (see tools/core070_postfit_policy_batch.R's header) showed that embedding one language's live runtime inside the other's child process is fragile (segfaults, unrelated fixtures reached transitively); JuliaCall is only a SUGGESTED R dependency (R/julia-bridge.R:1-9) and may not even be installed against the frozen library, so a literal round-trip test would non-portably gate this batch's executability on an optional package. This narrower, file/subprocess-based design still gives real coverage of the documented failure mode (family admission) and the documented success mode (fit correctness) without that fragility.

lognormal and truncated_poisson are EXECUTABLE_NOW as REJECTION-path cases, not numeric-parity cases: src/bridge.jl's _bridge_family_key DOES support both, but R's own .GLLVM_JULIA_BRIDGE_FAMILIES admission list (R/julia-bridge.R:18-30) does not, so the family is rejected before Julia is ever reached. This matches the manifest's own alternate comparand clause ('for unwired families: a documented, non-crashing rejection with a clear error surfaced to R') even though the underlying reason (an R-side allow-list gap, not a missing Julia fitter) differs from the manifest's original assumption ('no direct GLLVM.jl analytic-Laplace fitter yet') -- corrected here from directly reading both sides' source, per the task's 'verify existence by grepping the actual source before classifying' instruction.
